subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If y = a cos x + (b + 2x) sin x, show that y″ + y = 4 cos x.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.202, chapter 9 DIFFERENTIATION, Short Answer question 13. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which rule the second term needs and what happens when you add y at the end.

steps.label: Differentiate once
steps.margin_note: First mark. (b + 2x) sin x is a product of two functions of x, so the product rule is compulsory here — it is where most of the marks are lost.
lines: y = a cos x + (b + 2x) sin x
The second term is a product, so use the product rule:
y′ = −a sin x + [2 sin x + (b + 2x) cos x]

recall.must_convey: That the product rule is applied to (b + 2x) sin x, giving y′ = −a sin x + 2 sin x + (b + 2x) cos x.
accept: use the product rule on b plus two x times sin x
y dash is minus a sin x plus two sin x plus b plus two x cos x
differentiate the first factor times the second plus the first times the derivative of the second
product rule vaadali, rendo term product kabatti
the derivative of b plus two x is two

steps.why: a cos x differentiates on its own, but (b + 2x) sin x is a product, so it needs two terms. Missing one of them breaks every line after it.
common_mistakes: Writing the second term as 2 cos x, differentiating each factor separately.
Losing the minus sign on the derivative of a cos x.
steps.memory_tip: The product rule always produces TWO terms — count them before moving on.

steps.label: Differentiate a second time
steps.margin_note: Two marks — the longest step. The product rule is used a second time on (b + 2x) cos x, and that is where the second 2 cos x comes from.
lines: y″ = −a cos x + 2 cos x + [2 cos x − (b + 2x) sin x]
y″ = −a cos x + 4 cos x − (b + 2x) sin x

recall.must_convey: That differentiating again gives y″ = −a cos x + 4 cos x − (b + 2x) sin x.
accept: differentiate again using the product rule on b plus two x cos x
y double dash is minus a cos x plus four cos x minus b plus two x sin x
two cos x appears twice so it becomes four cos x
malli product rule vaadithe four cos x vasthundi
the sin term keeps the bracket b plus two x with a minus sign

steps.why: Two separate terms each contribute a 2 cos x — one from differentiating 2 sin x, one from the product rule on (b + 2x) cos x — and together they make the 4 cos x the question asks for.
common_mistakes: Getting 2 cos x instead of 4 cos x by using the product rule only once.
Writing the last term as +(b + 2x) sin x, forgetting that cos x differentiates to −sin x.
steps.memory_tip: The 4 in the answer is 2 + 2 — one 2 from each of the two places a 2 appears.

steps.label: Add y and cancel
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Write the two lines side by side before cancelling — the a cos x pair and the (b + 2x) sin x pair each cancel, and 4 cos x is all that is left.
lines: y″ + y = [−a cos x + 4 cos x − (b + 2x) sin x] + [a cos x + (b + 2x) sin x]
The −a cos x and a cos x cancel, and the two (b + 2x) sin x terms cancel

recall.must_convey: That adding y removes the a cos x and (b + 2x) sin x terms, leaving 4 cos x.
accept: add y and the a cos x terms cancel
the b plus two x sin x terms cancel as well
only four cos x is left so it is proved
y kalipithe rendu terms cancel ayi four cos x migulutundi
both constants a and b disappear from the answer

steps.why: The constants a and b must vanish, because the required answer 4 cos x contains neither. Their cancelling is the check that the two derivatives are right.
common_mistakes: Subtracting y instead of adding it.
Leaving a or b in the final line, which means an earlier sign is wrong.
steps.memory_tip: The result has no a and no b, so if either survives the cancelling, go back to y″.

insider_note: The second term is a product, so the product rule is needed at BOTH differentiations. Adding y back cancels the a and b terms entirely, leaving only the 4 cos x.
